lesson_title: Half a Pizza Still Has a Straight Side
hook_text: The #1 trap in Grade 10 measurement: a semicircle's edge is NOT half the circle's.
clip_script: The semicircle trap makes sense the moment you think about pizza. A full pizza has crust all the way around — that is the circumference. Take half the pizza: half the crust, sure. But run your finger around the edge of that half-pizza — curve, and then the straight cut edge. For the radius-3 bed: half the crust is 9,426 metres, the straight cut is the 6-metre diameter, so the full edge is 15,43 metres. Order only 9,43 and the bed lies open along its whole straight side. The topping never tricks anyone — half a pizza has half the topping. Area takes the fraction. Only the edge picks up straight sides. Curve plus cuts, every time.
visual_style: Overhead pizza animation: crust glowing as a finger traces it, the cut edge flashing red when forgotten, then metres labels snapping onto curve and diameter.
pacing: Quick setup, finger-trace suspense, satisfying numeric payoff.
